title: Postmortem: Stark Distribution proration overbilling

transcript.speaker: jordan@northwind.dev
transcript.text: Blameless postmortem, usual rules. Mei, walk us through it.

transcript.speaker: mei@northwind.dev
transcript.text: Stark Distribution added 8 leased robots on July 9. The legacy billing service prorated the add-on, but it also re-billed the full month for those units on the July 15 cycle. So they got charged twice for the partial period.

transcript.speaker: mei@northwind.dev
transcript.text: Root cause: the proration function used the contract anniversary date instead of the billing cycle date when a mid-cycle change crossed the 15th. Edge case that's been there since 2024 but only triggers on adds after the 1st and before the 15th.

transcript.speaker: omar@northwind.dev
transcript.text: From the customer side, their finance team caught it, opened a ticket, and their controller was not thrilled. The overcharge was a bit under eleven thousand dollars.

transcript.speaker: raj@northwind.dev
transcript.text: How fast did we fix it?

transcript.speaker: mei@northwind.dev
transcript.text: Ticket came in the 17th, I had the fix in review the 18th, deployed the 19th. That's BIL-31. Credit memo went out the 20th.

transcript.speaker: mei@northwind.dev
transcript.text: Yes. I ran a query across every invoice since January. Two other accounts hit it, but for under two hundred dollars each. Credits issued.

transcript.speaker: omar@northwind.dev
transcript.text: I'd like a short apology email to Stark that explains it in human terms. They appreciate transparency.

transcript.speaker: mei@northwind.dev
transcript.text: I'll draft the technical paragraph, you own the tone.

transcript.speaker: raj@northwind.dev
transcript.text: Bigger question. How many more of these are hiding in the legacy service?

transcript.speaker: mei@northwind.dev
transcript.text: Honestly? Probably a few. The proration code is 900 lines with no tests on half of it. PayStream does proration natively. That's the strongest argument for the migration.

transcript.speaker: raj@northwind.dev
transcript.text: Then let's accelerate it. I'd rather you spend Q3 on PayStream than patching edge cases.

transcript.speaker: jordan@northwind.dev
transcript.text: Agreed. I'll move the PayStream work up and take the reconciliation dashboard off Mei's plate.

transcript.speaker: mei@northwind.dev
transcript.text: Meanwhile I'll add regression tests for every proration path I can enumerate, and an alert when an invoice line exceeds the contract rate.

transcript.speaker: jordan@northwind.dev
transcript.text: Good. Mei, write the ADR for the migration so we have the decision on record. Thanks all.

summary: Stark Distribution was overbilled (just under $11k) for 8 robots added mid-cycle on July 9 because the legacy billing service's proration used the contract anniversary date instead of the billing cycle date. Mei Chen fixed it in BIL-31 (deployed July 19), audited all 2026 invoices, found two minor additional cases, and credits were issued. Team decided to accelerate the PayStream migration.
decisions: Accelerate the Billing v2 PayStream migration to Q3, prioritized above other billing work.
Add an invoice anomaly alert when a line exceeds the contracted rate.

action_items.text: Add regression tests for all proration paths in the legacy billing service
Write ADR-007 for the PayStream migration
Send Stark Distribution an apology and explanation email
Reprioritize Q3 roadmap to pull PayStream migration forward
